questions.text: In Listening L1, why does Rafi initially call the library help desk?
options: To report a lost membership card
To ask whether he can reserve a study room

meta.scriptText: Receptionist: City Library help desk, this is Mina speaking. How can I help? Rafi: Hi, I'd like to know if I can reserve a small study room for a group project this Thursday afternoon. Receptionist: Yes, small rooms can be booked for two hours at a time. How many people will be coming? Rafi: Four. We only need a whiteboard and a power socket for a laptop. Receptionist: That's fine. The first available slot after lunch is from 2:30 to 4:30. Rafi: That works well. Could you book it under Rafi Karim? Receptionist: Certainly. Can I also take your membership number? Rafi: Yes, it's 18426. Receptionist: Thank you. Please arrive ten minutes early, because if no one has checked in by the start time, the room may be offered to someone else. Rafi: Understood. Is food allowed inside? Receptionist: Water bottles are fine, but please keep snacks outside the room. Rafi: No problem. Thanks for your help.

questions.text: In Listening L2, what is the main problem discussed in the farm podcast?
options: The farm has too many workers during harvest season
Rainwater is running off quickly instead of soaking into the soil
Local customers prefer imported vegetables
The farm cannot store enough seeds for the next year
questions.correctAnswer: Rainwater is running off quickly instead of soaking into the soil
questions.explanation: The speaker explains that compact soil caused water to run across the surface instead of being absorbed.

meta.scriptTitle: Improving Water Retention on a Small Farm
meta.scriptText: Speaker: Today we're looking at a small vegetable farm outside Cumilla that struggled with water retention. After short periods of heavy rain, the top layer of soil became hard, and water moved across the field instead of sinking in. The farm team first assumed they needed to dig deeper drainage channels, but an agricultural adviser suggested a different approach. She noticed that repeated foot traffic and machine use had compacted the surface. Her advice was to reduce unnecessary movement across the beds, cover bare ground with organic mulch, and plant a fast-growing clover between crop rows after harvest. Within one season, the farm recorded slower runoff and improved moisture around young plants. The change did not eliminate irrigation, but it reduced the number of emergency watering sessions during hot weeks. The adviser also recommended keeping a simple field diary. Staff wrote down rainfall amounts, planting dates, and any visible changes in leaf colour. These notes helped them compare sections of the farm and identify where improvements were strongest.

questions.text: Complete the note from Listening L2: The adviser suggested planting ______ between crop rows after harvest.
questions.explanation: The speaker states that the adviser recommended planting fast-growing clover between crop rows after harvest.

questions.correctAnswer: To compare different parts of the farm over time

meta.scriptText: Adviser: Careers Office, Omar speaking. Nadia: Hello, I saw a poster about the employer networking session next Wednesday. Is registration still open? Adviser: Yes, but there are only a few spaces left in the afternoon group. Nadia: That's fine. I mainly want to speak to firms that offer marketing internships. Adviser: Then the 3 p.m. session should suit you. Three agencies and one retail brand will be there. Nadia: Great. Do I need to bring a printed CV? Adviser: A digital copy on your phone is acceptable, but many students still prefer to bring one printed copy. Nadia: I'll do that. Adviser: I also recommend arriving by 2:30 because there will be a short workshop on introducing yourself to employers. Nadia: That sounds useful. Can you register me under Nadia Rahman? Adviser: Of course. Could you confirm your student number? Nadia: It's 240918. Adviser: Done. You'll get a confirmation email with the room number this afternoon.

questions.text: In Listening L4, what is the lecturer mainly describing?
options: How a university reduced food waste in one semester
How students should choose their degree subjects
Why city buses are replacing campus bicycles
Why laboratories must remain open all night
questions.correctAnswer: How a university reduced food waste in one semester
questions.explanation: The talk focuses on the steps taken by the university to cut food waste in cafeterias and hostels.

meta.scriptText: Lecturer: This morning I'd like to outline a campus project that reduced food waste over one semester. The university began by measuring how much untouched food was leaving the main cafeteria each day. The average was 86 kilograms, which surprised many staff members. Instead of immediately changing the menu, the sustainability office first interviewed students and discovered two practical causes. Portions were often too large for evening diners, and many students had no idea that they could request half portions. The cafeteria therefore introduced smaller standard servings, clearer signs near the counters, and a discounted box for unsold meals during the final hour of service. In the hostels, student volunteers ran a weekly campaign on planning grocery shopping and storing fruit correctly. By the end of the semester, cafeteria waste had fallen by 28 percent. The university did not claim the problem had been solved completely, but the project showed that small behavioural changes, combined with better information, could make a measurable difference.

questions.explanation: The lecturer says the average was 86 kilograms per day.

questions.text: In Listening L5, what is the purpose of the community language exchange programme?
options: To help newcomers practise speaking with local volunteers
To prepare schoolchildren for science competitions
To train radio presenters in pronunciation
To replace formal language classes at the college
questions.correctAnswer: To help newcomers practise speaking with local volunteers
questions.explanation: The radio segment explains that the programme pairs newcomers with volunteers for informal speaking practice.

meta.scriptText: Presenter: You're listening to City Voices. Today we're discussing a community language exchange that started at the Riverside Learning Centre. Every Tuesday evening, local volunteers meet newcomers who want extra speaking practice in English. Coordinator: The idea is simple. Many learners attend formal classes, but they still need a relaxed space to ask questions, make mistakes, and build confidence. Presenter: How are the sessions organised? Coordinator: We start with a short activity, usually based on everyday topics such as shopping, transport, or health appointments. Then participants move into small groups. Each group has one volunteer and three or four learners. Presenter: Has attendance grown? Coordinator: Yes. We began with 12 learners last autumn, and now we usually have around 35. Presenter: What has made the programme successful? Coordinator: Consistency. We meet every week, and we also ask volunteers to keep a simple progress sheet so learners can see which situations they have practised. The centre is now looking for more volunteers with experience in customer service or community work, because they often know the kind of conversations newcomers need most.

questions.explanation: The presenter says the volunteers meet learners every Tuesday evening.
